title: Scale Readiness Sentinel Checklist and Probabilistic KPI Map
body:
Purpose:
This working brief combines a lightweight readiness checklist with a small probabilistic KPI map to help product ops decide whether to advance staged traffic during pilot->scale transitions. Focus is on three canonical risks we see in inference rollouts: latency tail growth, unit-cost regression, and adoption/quality drop (user-level errors or NPS fallback signals).

How to use this doc:
- Weekly snapshot used by launch commander and ops on-call.
- Fill the KPI observations section daily during pilot; update probability bands weekly.
- If any sentinel gate trips (red) escalate to SRE + Product within 1 hour.

Executive summary (one-line):
We only open the next traffic tranche when the combined posterior probability of critical failure across latency OR cost OR quality is < 12% at the tranche volume.

Readiness sentinel checklist (pre-tranche go/no-go):
1) Canary stability: 72h no P99 latency spike > baseline+30% AND error-rate <= baseline * 1.5. Owner: infra-sre.
2) Cost sanity: observed per-token cost within +/-10% of modeled estimate for the tranche given batching/quantization profile. Owner: finance-ops.
3) Quality check: automated eval set pass-rate >= 95% and top-3 human review sample CTR within expected band. Owner: applied-ml.
4) Fallbacks validated: model variant fallback, region fallback, and circuit-breaker tested in staging with <1s failover median. Owner: serving-runtime.
5) Oncall coverage: 24/7 pager rotation confirmed for 48h after tranche open. Owner: product-ops.
6) Communication: post-tranche status channel created, escalation list verified, key customers notified. Owner: GTM lead.

Probabilistic KPI map (how we convert signals -> go probability):
- Inputs observed daily: P99 latency (ms), error rate (%), per-token cost ($), eval pass-rate (%), ticket volume delta (tickets/day).
- For each metric compute a 3-band likelihood of critical failure for the tranche (Low/Medium/High) mapped to numeric probabilities: Low=5%, Medium=20%, High=60%.
- Combine metrics by taking the complement of the product of complements (assume independence for quick decision):
  combined_failure_prob = 1 - product(1 - metric_prob_i)
- Decision rule: proceed if combined_failure_prob < tranche_threshold. Default tranche_thresholds: 10% for conservative, 15% balanced, 25% aggressive.

Example (sample calculation) for tranche target of 100k requests/day:
- P99 latency: Medium -> 20%
- Error rate: Low -> 5%
- Cost deviation: Low -> 5%
- Eval drift: Medium -> 20%
Combined = 1 - (1-0.2)*(1-0.05)*(1-0.05)*(1-0.2) = 1 - 0.8*0.95*0.95*0.8 ≈ 1 - 0.577 ≈ 42.3% -> fail (above all thresholds).
Notes: if two metrics are correlated (e.g., latency & errors because of overloaded region), apply heuristic discount: treat the pair as max(prob_i, prob_j) instead of probabilistic product.

KPI observation template (copy into daily snapshot):
- Snapshot date:
- Tranche target (requests/day):
- Observed P50/P95/P99 latency (ms):
- Error rate (5xx+model failures) %:
- Per-token cost observed vs modeled ($, % delta):
- Eval pass-rate on golden set %:
- Human sample quality delta vs baseline (n=50):
- Ticket volume delta (tickets/day):
- Suggested metric band assignments (Latency:Low/Med/High, Errors:Low/Med/High, Cost:Low/Med/High, Eval:Low/Med/High):
- Computed combined_failure_prob: X%
- Decision: Proceed / Pause / Rollback - rationale + owner

Fallback playbook (quick actions if sentinel trips after tranche open):
- If combined_failure_prob > 40% and sustained over 30m: immediately redirect new traffic to previous stable model variant (automated route) and throttle new signups for 1h.
- If P99 > baseline*2 or error rate spikes > 3x: trigger blue/green rollback and spin up additional capacity in dedicated zone while monitoring for regression.
- If cost deviation > +25%: enable temporary quantization fallback profile and pause non-critical batching.
- Communication template: short status + next check interval + public-facing customer note draft (one paragraph) — owner: comms.

Operational runbook snippets (ops commands & tickets):
- Quick health checks: curl /health, kubectl top pods (serving namespace), stream token-level latency traces to console.
- Common Jira tickets to file: PRODOPS-ROLLBACK, PRODOPS-SCALE-INCIDENT, PRODOPS-COST-ALERT.
- Slack shortcuts: #prodops/launch-commander, /oncall escalate <name>.

Capacity and cost estimation anchor (for finance ops):
- Baseline: model A = 0.0009 $/token at 8-bit quant, expected avg tokens/request = 120, expected requests/day = tranche target.
- Modeled daily cost = requests/day * tokens/request * $/token. Example 100k * 120 * 0.0009 = $10,800/day.
- Include buffer: tranche reserve = modeled_daily_cost * 1.15 (15% buffer).

Open questions & unresolved items (for next iteration):
- We need a better correlation model between latency and error rate for region-level failures (SRE to own a short probe).
- Define exact gating for staged customer cohorts (enterprise customers may require stricter thresholds).
- Add small Bayesian update script to combine historical tranche outcomes into prior for the probabilistic map. (Owner: applied-ml).

Appendix: suggested daily snapshot cadence and owners:
- 09:00 PDT: product-ops post snapshot and suggested banding. Owner: Maya.
- 12:00 PDT: infra-sre health check and latency review. Owner: Alex.
- 16:00 PDT: applied-ml quality check and human sample. Owner: Priya.
- 18:30 PDT: gating decision updated; launch-commander confirms. Owner: Samir.

Quick links and references:
- Staging runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/staging-runbook
- Cost model workbook (read-only): https://sheets.redwood.ai/d/finance-model-2025
- Pager rota: https://oncall.redwood.ai/rota/product-ops

Status notes:
- This doc is an in-review working brief intended to be copied into a daily snapshot template (use the KPI observation template). Expect iterations as we gather two full tranche cycles.
